name: Saul and the witch of Endor
charge: Seeking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, after cutting them off out of the land himself
summary: With the Philistines encamped and the Lord not answering him by dreams, by Urim, or by prophets, Saul disguised himself, went by night to a woman at Endor, and asked her to bring up Samuel. He had himself put the mediums out of the land. He was told he and his sons would be with Samuel the next day, fell on the earth, and died on Gilboa. Chronicles names this as a cause of his death.
offense: Saul had removed those with familiar spirits and wizards from the land. When the Philistine host frightened him and the Lord answered neither by dreams, Urim, nor prophets, he sought a woman with a familiar spirit himself (1 Samuel 28:3-7). He knew the prohibition because he had enforced it. The silence he encountered did not give him permission to seek an answer by a forbidden means. He disguised himself and went by night. The woman feared a trap because of Saul's own earlier action, but he swore by the Lord that no punishment would come upon her for the deed (1 Samuel 28:8-10). The name of the Lord was invoked to reassure someone in the performance of what his law condemned. An oath cannot make disobedience holy. Leviticus 19:31 forbids seeking familiar spirits; Deuteronomy 18:10-12 forbids the necromancer and places these practices among the abominations Israel was to reject. Saul sought counsel while continuing the course for which counsel had condemned him. His need was not another voice agreeing to direct him, but obedience to the word already received.
judgment: Samuel's answer did not open another course. The Lord had departed from Saul and had done what was previously announced: torn the kingdom from him and given it to David. The refusal to execute the word against Amalek was named again (1 Samuel 28:15-18). Going to the forbidden source had not removed the command he had rejected.
